To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the insertion of marginally-hydrophobic helices into the endoplasic reticulum depends on their context, and that the context is often sufficient to ensure the correct insertion of the helix.
most of the marginally-hydrophobic helices do not insert into the ER membrane by themselves and that flanking loops or nearest-neighbor TM helices are sufficient to ensure their insertion.

most of the marginally-hydrophobic transmembranous helices from membrane proteins do not insert into the endoplismatic reticulum membrane when expressed by themselves, and that loops and neighboring transmembranuous helices are sufficient to ensure insertion of many of these helices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
membrane insertion of marginally and nonhydrophobic transmembranous helices and their influence by neighboring helices.
the insertion of marginally amphipathic TMHs into the endoplasic reticulum membrane.
a new aspect of the insertion process, namely the role of the sequence context of marginally hydrophylic TMHs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the insertion of marginally and non-hydrophobic TMH is a complex process involving both flanking loops and TMHs as well as post-insertion rearrangements.
the membrane insertion of marginally helical TMHs is a complex process that depends on both the sequence of the helix itself and the context provided by the neighboring TMHs and loops.
the membrane insertion of a marginally helix depends on its local environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the insertion of marginally helices depends on their context, which is in line with the idea that membrane proteins fold cotranslationally.
the membrane insertion efficiency of marginally hydrophilic TMHs can be influenced by the local sequence environment.
most marginally hydrophobics TMHs are efficiently inserted into the endosomal membrane by their local environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the translocon is able to recognize marginally hydrophobics TMHs if the local context allows it.
the membrane insertion of marginally amphipathic TMHs depends on the context in which they are embedded.
the insertion of marginally helices is not a random process but is strongly influenced by the context of their insertion.
